description: Routing eval for the verification seam introduced by the verification-engineer agent (ROLE-004). verification-engineer, sde-fullstack, code-reviewer, and root-cause all answer to check/test/verify/confirm vocabulary. The boundaries: verification-engineer independently EXECUTES checks against explicit criteria and returns a pass/fail/inconclusive verdict; sde-fullstack implements (and self-verifies) changes; code-reviewer judges a diff WITHOUT running it; root-cause diagnoses WHY an observed failure happens. Positives name the intended member; negatives share the verify/check vocabulary but must route to none of them.
notes: Seeded 2026-07-29 with ROLE-004; no baseline captured yet. The suite caveat binds hard here: three of the four members are AGENTS, whose positives under-fire in headless one-shot mode — trust the negatives and cross-run regressions over absolute agent-positive rates. Tightest seams: 'verify the fix' (verification-engineer) vs 'fix it and add a test' (sde-fullstack); 'read the diff, don't run it' (code-reviewer) vs 'run it and report' (verification-engineer); 'is it actually fixed' (verification-engineer) vs 'why is it failing' (root-cause). Negatives rely on the documented whole-cluster default for expect_not_fires; no deliberate narrowing exists in this cluster.

cases.prompt: We just landed a fix for the pagination off-by-one on this branch. Independently verify it actually works: reproduce the original failure, run the acceptance and regression checks, and give me a pass/fail verdict I can release on.
cases.expected_output: Independent execution against explicit criteria ending in a release verdict — the verifier's remit exactly, and 'independently' plus 'reproduce the original failure' is its trigger vocabulary. Agent positive: read under the headless under-fire caveat.

cases.prompt: Before I cut the release, independently run the acceptance checks for the CSV export feature against the criteria in the ticket and tell me pass, fail, or inconclusive — and name the exact revision you tested.
cases.expected_output: Acceptance execution with the verifier's own verdict triad and revision-binding named in the request. Agent positive: read under the headless under-fire caveat.

cases.prompt: Look over the diff on this branch for bugs and security issues — don't run anything, just read the changes and give me a merge verdict.
cases.expected_output: A diff judged without execution — code-reviewer's side of the seam, made explicit by 'don't run anything'. Agent positive: read under the headless under-fire caveat.

cases.prompt: Our nightly sync job started timing out three days ago and nobody knows why. Figure out what's causing it.
cases.expected_output: An observed failure whose CAUSE is unknown — root-cause's loop, not a verification pass. 'Figure out what's causing it' separates diagnosis from 'tell me whether it works'.

cases.prompt: The date parser rejects ISO week dates like 2026-W31-3. Fix it and add a regression test so it stays fixed.
cases.expected_output: Implementation with its own test — the builder's remit. 'Add a regression test' is the decoy overlap with the verifier; the deliverable is the fix, which the verifier is prohibited from writing. Agent positive: read under the headless under-fire caveat.

cases.prompt: After last night's power blip, verify all the services in my lab came back up and are healthy.
cases.expected_output: Live-lab health, not repository verification — homelab-platform (with lab-audit for hygiene) owns this, and neither is a member. 'Verify' is the decoy vocabulary.

cases.prompt: Add a verification stage to our GitHub Actions pipeline that runs the acceptance suite on every PR.
cases.expected_output: CI pipeline authoring — the ci-actions skill's remit, not a one-time verification. 'Verification stage' and 'acceptance suite' are the decoy vocabulary; the deliverable is workflow YAML.

cases.prompt: Verify whether Postgres 16 still supports the recovery.conf file before we design our backup tooling around it.
cases.expected_output: An evidence question answered from sources — researcher's remit, not test execution. 'Verify whether X supports Y' is research; there is nothing to run and no acceptance criteria to grade.
